title: Elements and Compounds as Pure Substances
competency: Describe the properties of pure substances as: having fixed chemical composition, examples of which are elements and compounds; and that all the atoms of an element have a unique number of protons.
objectives: Define pure substances and identify their key characteristics.
Explain the concept of fixed chemical composition in compounds.
Recognize that the number of protons (atomic number) is unique to every element.
introduction: In the world of chemistry, matter is classified based on its purity. While many things we see are mixtures, some substances are 'pure.' Pure substances have a constant composition and distinct properties that do not change. These are further divided into two groups: elements and compounds.
content:
1. What is a Pure Substance?

A Pure Substance is a form of matter that has a constant (fixed) chemical composition and characteristic properties. Unlike mixtures, you cannot separate a pure substance into other types of matter using physical means like filtering or boiling.

2. Elements: The Simplest Form

An Element is a pure substance that consists of only one type of atom. It cannot be broken down into simpler substances by chemical means.

  • Unique Protons: The most important property of an element is that all its atoms have the same number of protons in the nucleus. This is called the Atomic Number. No two different elements have the same number of protons.

3. Compounds: Chemically Combined

A Compound is a pure substance made of two or more different elements that are chemically bonded together.

  • Fixed Composition: Compounds always contain the same elements in the same fixed proportion by mass. For example, pure water is always made of 2 hydrogen atoms and 1 oxygen atom (H2O). If you change the ratio, you change the substance.
  • New Properties: A compound has physical and chemical properties that are different from the elements that make it up.

examples.title: Elements (Pure Atoms)
examples.description: Gold (Au) consists only of gold atoms, each having 79 protons. Oxygen (O2) consists only of oxygen atoms, each having 8 protons.

examples.title: Compounds (Fixed Ratios)
examples.description: Table Salt (NaCl) is a compound. It is always 50% Sodium and 50% Chlorine by atom count. Even though Sodium is a reactive metal and Chlorine is a toxic gas, their compound (Salt) is safe to eat.

keyTerms.definition: Matter that has a uniform and definite composition.
The force of attraction that holds atoms together in a compound.
The number of protons in the nucleus which defines the identity of an element.

keyConcepts: Pure substances include both elements and compounds.
The identity of an element is determined solely by its number of protons.
Compounds are formed in fixed ratios and can only be separated by chemical reactions.
summary: Pure substances are categorized into elements and compounds. Elements are made of one type of atom with a unique number of protons. Compounds are made of different elements chemically combined in fixed ratios. Both are distinct from mixtures because their chemical composition is constant.

selfCheck.q: What defines the unique identity of an element?
Can a compound be separated into its elements by filtering it?
selfCheck.a: No, it can only be separated by chemical means/reactions.

selfCheck.q: Why is water (H2O) considered a pure substance and not a mixture?
selfCheck.a: Because it has a fixed chemical composition that is always the same.
